title: Min Stack
oneLinerQuestion: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in O(1) time.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Min Stack design problem requires implementing a stack that supports standard LIFO operations (push, pop, top) along with retrieving the minimum element (getMin) in strict O(1) time. While a standard stack can push, pop, and inspect the top in constant time, finding the minimum typically requires scanning all elements in O(N) time. Storing a single global scalar for the minimum fails when that minimum is popped, as there is no record of the preceding minimum. By pairing the primary data stack with a parallel auxiliary stack ('minStack'), each level of the auxiliary stack records the minimum value present in the stack up to that exact depth. Thus, popping an element automatically restores the prior minimum at the top of the auxiliary stack in O(1) time.

- Step 1: Data Structure Initialization — We initialize two separate stacks: `this.stack = []` (storing actual data elements) and `this.minStack = []` (recording the running minimum corresponding to each height).

- Step 2: Implementing push(val) — We push `val` directly onto `this.stack`. To update the minimum tracking, if `this.minStack` is empty, we push `val` onto `this.minStack`. Otherwise, we compare `val` against the current top of `minStack` and push the smaller of the two: `this.minStack.push(Math.min(val, this.minStack[this.minStack.length - 1]))`. Both stacks always maintain identical lengths.

- Step 3: Implementing pop() — Because both stacks are maintained in lockstep synchronization, removing an element requires popping from both: `this.stack.pop()` and `this.minStack.pop()`. This cleanly discards the element and its associated running minimum, automatically exposing the previous minimum at the top of `minStack`.

- Step 4: Implementing top() — We return the element at the top of the primary data stack without removing it: `return this.stack[this.stack.length - 1]`.

- Step 5: Implementing getMin() — The minimum element of the entire stack is always located at the top of the auxiliary stack: `return this.minStack[this.minStack.length - 1]`. This achieves immediate O(1) retrieval without inspecting any other elements.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(1) strictly for all operations (push, pop, top, getMin), as array end accesses and scalar comparisons run in constant time. Space Complexity: O(N) auxiliary space, where N is the total number of elements pushed, required to store the parallel running minimum entries.
pseudoCode:
CLASS MinStack:
    CONSTRUCTOR(): stack = [], minStack = []
    FUNCTION push(val):
        val = MIN(val, IS_EMPTY(minStack) ? val : TOP(minStack))
        PUSH val TO stack
        PUSH val TO minStack
    FUNCTION pop(): POP stack; POP minStack
    FUNCTION top(): RETURN TOP(stack)
    FUNCTION getMin(): RETURN TOP(minStack)
END CLASS
